source.title: Attribution-Guided Distillation of Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Cristina P. Martin-Linares; Jonathan P. Ling

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a DMSAE result on an absorption benchmark, but does not directly test parent-child firing gaps or whether changing dictionary size or sparsity fixes them.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses feature splitting and absorption as background and reports an absorption benchmark outcome for DMSAEs. It does not report an experiment measuring whether larger dictionaries replace coarse features with input-partitioning, nearby-direction features. Its other results on core selection and transfer across training cycles do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper introducing Distilled Matryoshka SAEs (DMSAEs). Its only absorption-related result is its own method's SAEBench absorption score against Matryoshka and BatchTopK baselines (Fig. 4, Fig. 7). That is a benchmark of the study's own method, not a test of whether absorption arises or persists across size or sparsity. All SAEs are 65k wide; there is no dictionary-size sweep and no parent/child firing analysis. Feature splitting and absorption appear only as cited background (Bricken 2023, Chanin 2024, Leask 2025).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that attribution-guided distillation yields a reusable 197-latent core of encoder directions that transfers across sparsity levels. They report that it improves several SAEBench metrics (notably absorption and RAVEL) over Matryoshka SAE baselines. They also note that AutoInterp drops sharply at the lowest sparsities. They make no claim about the feature-splitting pattern itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Matryoshka SAEs with an attribution-guided core-selection and transfer procedure; it does not conduct the dictionary-size splitting measurement described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Core carryover varies with the sparsity target: the authors report little carryover at k=20–80, substantial carryover at k=160 and k=320, and degenerate optimization at k=640.

fits_no_version.finding: DMSAE (Matryoshka SAE with a frozen 197-latent attribution-distilled core) matches or improves the SAEBench absorption score relative to Matryoshka SAE baselines across k=20–640 on Gemma-2-2B layer 12. Values appear only in Fig. 4, and the sparse-core variant shows similar trends (Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Freezing a distilled core of encoder directions in Matryoshka SAEs reduces measured absorption relative to standard Matryoshka SAEs.

record.problems: The absorption result is described qualitatively in the text, with exact values only in a figure; the study does not directly test the parent-child firing behavior or dictionary-size effect named in V4.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results concern core selection, reconstruction, attribution coverage, and training-cycle carryover; they do not measure the behaviors in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Not tested: there is no dictionary-size sweep, since all SAEs are 65k wide.
Not tested: only Gemma-2-2B layer 12 is studied, with no replication of splitting.
Not tested: there is no analysis of feature families or hierarchy geometry.
Not tested: there is no parent/child firing-gap analysis, and no test of whether size or sparsity changes fix absorption. Absorption is reported only as a benchmark score for the authors' own method.
Not tested: there is no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no count of novel latents.
Not tested: there is no direct measurement of splitting under different objectives. The absorption benchmark comparison is the authors' own method evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's guesses of T5 and a V4 link are overridden. The absorption result is the study's own method benchmarked against baselines, with numbers only in a figure, so it is T4. Core carryover across cycles depends on k (high at 160 and 320, low at 20–80, collapse at 640), but this concerns core stability rather than splitting.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of dictionary size measuring feature replacement, input coverage, or direction similarity.
Only Gemma-2-2B layer 12 is studied; no large-model or open-release replication of the splitting pattern.
No measurement of nested feature families, geometric closeness, or correspondence to a concept hierarchy.
The study reports an absorption benchmark result, but does not directly measure parent-child firing gaps or establish whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes them.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents and no measurement of novel latents.
No direct feature-splitting outcome is reported for the Matryoshka or DMSAE training objective.

rows.subject: DMSAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared the absorption benchmark metric with Matryoshka SAE baselines across target sparsities.
rows.value: The authors state that DMSAE matches or improves several metrics, particularly absorption; exact absorption values are shown in Figure 4.
rows.note: The reported aggregate statement does not establish whether parent latents fail to fire where child latents take over, or whether size or sparsity changes fix that behavior.
rows.check: The row compares the study's own method (DMSAE) with baseline SAEs on the SAEBench absorption score. It does not measure whether absorption occurs or whether changing size or sparsity fixes it, so it should not link to V4. Values exist only in Figure 4, with the text saying only that DMSAE 'matches or improves several metrics, particularly absorption'. Baseline values come from SAEBench releases rather than the authors' own runs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
